reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Endocrine Society clinical guidance
clinicalPearls: Characterised by asymmetric gonads, classically a dysgenetic testis on one side and a streak gonad on the other, in the context of 45,X/46,XY mosaicism
The phenotype is highly variable, ranging from apparently female through ambiguous genitalia to apparently male, depending on the functional testicular tissue present
Mullerian structures may persist on the side of the streak gonad because local anti-mullerian hormone is deficient there
Individuals may share features of Turner syndrome, such as short stature and cardiac or renal anomalies, when the 45,X line predominates
Dysgenetic gonads and streak gonads containing Y material carry a significant risk of gonadoblastoma, so gonadectomy of dysgenetic gonadal tissue is generally recommended
Prenatal detection of the mosaic karyotype often reveals a phenotypically normal male, illustrating the phenotypic breadth
Management addresses sex assignment, hormone replacement, growth, associated Turner-related anomalies and tumour prevention
reference.pathophysiology: Mixed gonadal dysgenesis arises from a 45,X/46,XY mosaic karyotype in which the proportion and distribution of the two cell lines vary between tissues. Where sufficient 46,XY cells populate the gonadal ridge, partial testicular differentiation occurs, whereas predominance of the 45,X line produces a streak gonad. The asymmetric hormone output determines internal and external genital development locally: the side with functional testicular tissue may show wolffian development and partial virilisation with mullerian regression, while the streak side retains mullerian structures. The retained Y-bearing dysgenetic and streak gonads are predisposed to gonadoblastoma and other germ cell tumours, and coexisting features of Turner syndrome may occur when the 45,X line is widespread.
additionalDifferentials: Turner syndrome and its mosaic variants
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (in a virilised infant)
additionalInvestigations: Karyotype on multiple tissues to detect and quantify 45,X/46,XY mosaicism
Pelvic and gonadal imaging by ultrasound or MRI to define gonads and mullerian structures
Serum gonadotropins, testosterone and anti-mullerian hormone, with hCG stimulation as needed
Gonadal biopsy and histology to characterise dysgenetic and streak tissue
Cardiac and renal imaging for Turner-associated anomalies
Germ cell tumour surveillance of retained gonadal tissue
redFlags: An enlarging gonadal mass suggesting gonadoblastoma or dysgerminoma
Undiagnosed cardiac or renal malformation associated with the 45,X line
Ambiguous genitalia in a newborn requiring multidisciplinary evaluation
Failure of pubertal progression from gonadal insufficiency
reference.prognosis: Outcome depends on the degree of gonadal function, the presence of Turner-related anomalies and the timing of gonadectomy; short stature and gonadal insufficiency are common. Early removal of dysgenetic Y-bearing gonads markedly reduces the substantial germ cell tumour risk.
pitfalls: Assuming a single karyotype excludes mosaicism when multiple tissues should be sampled
Leaving dysgenetic or streak gonads with Y material in situ and overlooking tumour risk
Missing associated cardiac and renal anomalies linked to the 45,X line
Predicting phenotype from karyotype alone rather than assessing gonadal function
references: Endocrine Society clinical practice guidance on disorders of sex development
management: Determine sex of rearing through multidisciplinary discussion with the family, involving paediatric endocrinology, urology, clinical genetics and psychology
Perform gonadectomy of dysgenetic and streak Y-bearing gonads to remove the substantial gonadoblastoma and germ cell tumour risk
Induce and maintain puberty and secondary sexual characteristics with sex-steroid replacement matched to the assigned sex
Consider growth-promoting therapy such as growth hormone where Turner-associated short stature is present
Undertake reconstructive genital surgery where indicated, timed and decided jointly with the family
Screen for and manage Turner-associated cardiac and renal anomalies with echocardiography and renal imaging
Provide genetic counselling on the 45,X/46,XY mosaic karyotype together with long-term fertility, hormonal and psychological support
